content.title: FORECAST FIRST ALERT: Snow tapers down but winds will cause blowing and drifting
content.text: Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 0:00Remaining Time 0:00 A BLIZZARD WARNING IS IN EFFECT FOR CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN MINNESOTA AND NORTHWEST WISCONSIN THROUGH EARLY MONDAY. THIS DOES INCLUDE THE TWIN CITIES.Snowfall as of 9 a.m. around the Twin Cities mostly ranges from 4″ to 7″ in the suburbs north of the downtown areas to 6″ to 9″ inside the 494/694 loop and 6″ to 10″ in the suburbs south of the Minnesota River. Highest Snowfall amounts of 12″ to 14″ occurred with Thunder Snow from Rochester and northeast into Wisconsin with over 16″ at Durand, Wisconsin.RELATED: Snow totals: 5-12 inches around Twin Cities metro, 20+ in other areasAn Additional 2″ to 4″ expected on top of what has already fallen can be expected Today in the Twin Cities for Total Storm Totals Ranging from 6″ to 12″ with an average of about 9″ in the Metro area. Snow will taper to Flurries this evening but Gusty Northwest Winds at 20 to 40 mph will cause Low Visibility and Blowing and Drifting Snow into Monday morning.See the latest forecast from Minnesota’s Weather AuthorityIt will be Cold Today with highs around 30 Degrees but feeling like the Teens with the Winds from the Northwest at 20 to 40 mph. Colder Tonight with nasty Wind-Chills at -5 to -15 Below and actual temperatures by Monday morning at 5 Degrees with Northwest Winds at 10 to 20 mph. Sunshine Monday afternoon but Cold and Windy with highs around 20 Degrees and Winds from the Northwest at 10 to 20 mph producing Winds-Chills of 0 to 5 Above during the afternoon. Lighter Winds Monday night with lows near 2 Degrees by Tuesday morning and Wind-Chills -5 to -10 Below.The Minnesota Department of Transportation has issued a No Travel Advisory for all state highways and Interstate 90 in multiple areas of southern Minnesota. Blowing snow and strong winds are creating blizzard conditions and are making travel difficult in the area.The advisory includes state highways and Interstate 90 in multiple counties: Blue Earth, Brown, Cottonwood, Faribault, Jackson, Le Sueur, Martin, Nicollet, Nobles, Rock, Sibley, Waseca, Watonwan, Chippewa, Lincoln, Lyon, Murray, Redwood, Renville, Pipestone, Yellow Medicine, Dodge, Fillmore, Freeborn, Goodhue, Houston, Mower, Olmsted, Rice, Steele, Wabasha and Winona.Motorists are advised not to travel in the region until conditions improve.Do not attempt longer drives during this blizzard. Heavy snow rates and strong winds will combine to make roads snow-covered, and visibility very low. Even in the metro areas, this is the type of storm where you only see brake lights in front of you on the highway at the last possible moment. Stay home if you can.When you clear the snow, do it in a few rounds. Even if you have a big two-stage snowblower, you are going to need to break it up into a couple rounds. I would recommend doing it once when you wake up Sunday, and then one more time in the afternoon. Chances are, you will need to do it one more time before work Monday.Roads could still be slippery during the Monday morning commute. I bet we see some school cancellations in rural areas, too. Following the snow, it will be very cold on Monday and Tuesday. Highs in the teens are likely Monday, and St Patrick’s Day begins below zero in the Twin Cities.This is a storm with the potential to impact a large portion of Minnesota and western Wisconsin — and we will continue tracking it closely as it approaches. Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 0:00Remaining Time 0:00 Road conditions declineDue to the storm, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz declared a peacetime emergency, authorizing the Minnesota National Guard to provide support for emergency operations.“Despite recent Spring weather, Minnesotans know that a March snowstorm is never out of the question,” said Gov. Walz. “As we brace for this potentially dangerous round of winter weather, I am grateful to our National Guard for stepping in to keep Minnesotans safe.” The cities of Minneapolis and St. Paul declared snow emergencies, which will begin at 9 p.m. on Sunday.
